evidence.quote: The RSI-PDE harness structures an agent’s numerical exploration while keeping its foundation model and executable supervisor fixed. Its accepted state is (P,\pi,M) : P is a modular solver with an identification router, equation-class modules and shared helpers; \pi is a model-written instruction policy for subsequent investigation; and M stores reusable numerical lessons. Figure 3 shows how that state moves through one round. Figure 4 separately follows the physical identification and refinement loop.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: Accepted solver edits carry their corresponding policy and memory updates into the next round. Rejected candidates return their numerical errors and rejection reasons, while remaining in the audit history. Algorithm 1 summarizes this process. The solver, policy and memory evolve; the displayed experiments do not promote self-modified executable supervisors. Establishing improvement of the controller itself would require equal-budget paired continuations from the same starting solver and memory.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: After development, an independent evaluator scores the frozen retained program on hidden cases. For a combined learning curve at round r , each group contributes its retained program after r validation submissions, or its final program if it stopped earlier. Thus a round is a submission index, not a common elapsed-time budget, and summed group submissions differ from the final index of a combined curve. Hidden checkpoint scores are assembled for reporting and do not return to the running agent.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: The model weights and executable supervisor remain fixed, while solver code, policy text and memory can change. Final-program improvement does not establish that an evolved controller is a better improver; that claim requires matched continuation experiments. Recorded calls decrease in eight of 12 comparisons, with substantial exceptions on Noisy. Dollar costs depend on token usage and caching, and selected costs use retrospective stop-rule replay while retaining full-budget scores. Those estimates require fresh stopped runs before they can support jointly achieved accuracy/cost claims.

evidence.quote: Actor harness H and Evaluator harness \Phi contain instructions, working rubrics, and skills. Rubrics express checks against public requirements: Actor rubrics guide execution and self-checks; Evaluator rubrics guide assessment. Skills specify execution or verification procedures. H also includes persistent check plans, distinct from temporary trial questions. Model weights, task requirements, permissions, editor, selector, and reviewer instructions, eligibility, and acceptance rules remain fixed.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: A verification finding identifies a potential improvement, but the proposed harness must be tested through execution. Following harness optimization ( Pan et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ) , Step 1 runs the current Actor H and proposed Actor \widetilde{H} to produce fresh candidates a and b . Both receive the same temporary checks; only the proposal uses persistent edits. This exposes both Actors to the current verification concerns while testing the proposed execution procedure. Temporary checks expire after the round unless reconsidered. Without a proposal, both attempts use H .
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: Actor adoption requires support for the proposal’s own fresh candidate. Let V_{A} denote a valid trial of a changed Actor. Indicators s_{1},s_{2} record strict support in the initial comparison (or candidate-set selection) and the subsequent incumbent comparison, each requiring agreement in both presentation orders: H^{+}=\begin{cases}\widetilde{H},&V_{A}\land(z^{+}=b)\land s_{1}\land s_{2},\\ H,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} (5) Condition z^{+}=b requires selection of the proposal’s own output; s_{1}\land s_{2} excludes fallback choices. Selecting an earlier output leaves the Actor unchanged. This rule holds across main experiments and ablations (Appendix B.1 ).
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: To carry a verification finding into later attempts, Step 4 translates it into a proposed change to execution, verification, or both. The fixed editor \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{edit}} specifies an expected effect and a corresponding check for the next trial. Retrieving a supposedly unavailable contact sheet (Figure 2 ), for example, supplies an Actor retrieval instruction and an Evaluator check for future unavailability claims. The same observation can therefore provide both execution guidance and a verification procedure.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: Together, these findings explain the value of evolving verification alongside task execution. Active verification supplies evidence, co-evolution turns findings into execution guidance and reusable checks, and separate retention distinguishes successful outputs from supported updates. Task requirements and model weights stay fixed; adaptation changes how the agent executes, checks completion, and carries verification findings into subsequent attempts. More broadly, VbD suggests that test-time agent improvement can progress beyond choosing among existing behaviors by evolving the procedures that produce and evaluate feedback.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: Limitations VbD relies on observable evidence and model-based judgments. The Actor, Evaluator, and reviewer may share errors in interpreting evidence, so active verification and comparative review cannot eliminate incorrect selections or updates ( Wang et al., 2026a ) . Repeated trials require states or artifacts that can be isolated and inspected. As with replay-based adaptation ( Pan et al., 2026 ) , irreversible actions and environments that cannot be reset limit direct application. Delayed effects or inaccessible state may also escape verification. Our experiments evaluate three-round adaptation within individual tasks. Transfer across tasks and sustained improvement over longer evolution remain untested. Additional execution, verification, and harness revision incur inference and tool-use costs; deployment latency also depends on environment response times.

evidence.quote: Prior to full-scale benchmarking, we conducted a preliminary prompt-optimization study comparing three human-authored prompts, an OpenAI-optimized prompt [ 22 ] , and prompts compiled programmatically via DSPy MIPROv2 [ 19 , 20 ] and GEPA [ 21 ] ; because the DSPy GEPA optimizer achieved the highest pilot performance (69.60 EM and 80.70 \mathrm{F1}_{\mathrm{reported}} against SQuAD references), we standardized on this GEPA-compiled prompt across all subsequent zero-shot evaluations.

evidence.quote: We adapted the three open-weight models for one epoch over the 87,000-example training split using assistant-response cross-entropy supervision and the 8-bit AdamW optimizer. Llama 3 8B was fine-tuned via LoRA with Unsloth [ 23 , 34 ] ; gpt-oss-20b used 4-bit quantization with LoRA; and Llama 3.3 70B employed QLoRA with 4-bit NF4 quantization, BF16 compute, rank-stabilized LoRA [ 24 ] , cosine learning-rate scheduling, a warmup ratio of 0.03 , and weight decay of 0.01 . Table III summarizes the hyperparameter configurations.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: VI-B Limitations of our Research Our semantic-equivalence and passage-support assessments rely on one external LLM judge ( gpt-6-luna ) and therefore we interpret SES and RVS as judge-based diagnostic scores rather than independently verified measures of answer correctness. Responses accepted despite failing benchmark criteria identify cases for further examination, but do not by themselves establish annotation errors or model hallucination rates. Using a judge that generated none of the evaluated responses avoids direct self-evaluation [ 4 , 25 ] . Moreover, while our untuned-versus-fine-tuned comparisons isolate the exact lexical gains of parameter-efficient adaptation across all three open-weight models, we executed per-example SES and RVS assessments only on the zero-shot closed-weight frontier cohort. Extending these diagnostics to the untuned open-weight models (particularly their 1,268–1,647 \mathcal{F}_{N}^{\mathrm{ans}} cases and 1,447–2,558 \mathcal{F}_{P} cases), together with independent human adjudication, would help examine the contributions of formatting divergence and comprehension errors to their lexical deficit that we defer to future studies as mentioned below.

evidence.quote: Training and validation examples were used for prompt development and optimization without updating router model weights. Test examples were used for classification evaluation. The exclusions affected the reasoning training and validation partitions, removing six training examples and one validation example. The training and validation partitions for RAG, Web Search, and Calculator remained unchanged. One excluded reasoning training example had been selected as a DSPy few-shot demonstration for the 3B and 14B routers. The corresponding prompt artifacts therefore reflect development before the consistency audit. Recomputing metrics on the retained test records does not remove the influence of this demonstration. Results for these configurations are interpreted with this limitation. The RQ3 benchmark contains 127 pharmaceutical regulatory questions, each with a reference answer and four capability annotations. It evaluates routing on a domain-specific workload rather than establishing generalization across domains. Some questions also occur in the RQ1/RQ2 datasets. Table 2 reports annotation agreement for comparable overlapping question-capability pairs before label harmonization.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: Four Qwen2.5 models were used as routers to evaluate RQ1 and RQ2: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Qwen2.5-14B ( Yang et al., 2024 ) . Using models from the same family reduces architectural variation and enables comparisons of router capacity. All models were executed through Ollama in Google Colab using an NVIDIA T4 GPU. For each model, routing was evaluated independently for reasoning, RAG, web search, and calculator use under five prompting strategies: Minimal Baseline, Descriptive SME, DSPy Baseline, DSPy Few-Shot, and GEPA. The Minimal Baseline contained only the essential classification instruction and output constraint. The Descriptive SME prompt introduced manually designed capability-selection rules, while DSPy-based methods employed structured prompting and optimized few-shot demonstrations ( Khattab et al., 2024 ) . GEPA further optimized the routing instructions through a generator-evaluator process ( Agrawal et al., 2025 ) . RQ1 was evaluated by comparing the four router sizes under the same Minimal Baseline prompt, thereby isolating the effect of model capacity. RQ2 was evaluated by comparing prompting strategies within each router size and capability. Where prompt optimization required training or validation examples, only the designated training and validation partitions were used, while final performance was measured on the corrected held-out test sets. The RQ1/RQ2 workflow is illustrated in Figure 2 .
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: These findings require two qualifications. First, BERTScore measures semantic similarity to reference answers and does not establish factual, numerical, or regulatory correctness ( Zhang et al., 2020 ) . The small differences in mean scores also do not demonstrate statistical equivalence. Second, the reported downstream savings exclude router overhead, which increased with router capacity. Router and downstream latency were measured separately in Google Colab and AWS Bedrock, respectively. The results therefore characterize downstream computational savings and routing overhead under the evaluated conditions, rather than establishing an overall latency advantage for the 14B configuration.
evidence.quote_normalization: BeautifulSoup text, math replaced by alttext, whitespace folded

evidence.quote: The scope of the downstream benchmark further limits generalization. The benchmark contains 127 questions concerning pharmaceutical regulation, of which only ten are labeled as requiring web search. Broader workloads and task-specific correctness assessments are needed to determine whether the observed trade-offs persist beyond this setting. Evaluating the complete pipeline under a controlled deployment would also clarify when downstream savings outweigh the additional computational cost of a larger router.
